quotation marks and `mark`/`p` fields. No scansion flags in the packet, so no hand-scan was called for. `t` untouched

## The drafter's doubts, resolved

- **ἀμήχανος (167)**: kept "impossible to deal with" in `i`, "past all dealing with" in `l`. From the grammar, ἀ-μήχανος "without μηχανή" is active ("resourceless", Odyssey 19.363 "helpless") or passive ("that nothing can be done about"); the Iliad table already takes the passive sense for ἀμήχανα ἔργα (8.130), and the context (Diomedes' complaint that Nestor will not be managed, not that he is without means, with a man of Nestor's resource) fits only the passive. "Helpless" refused: it says the opposite of the point.
- **σχέτλιε (164)**: nominative predicate σχέτλιός ἐσσι, not a vocative; "cruel" in `l` and `i` follows the table (σχέτλιος "cruel", vocative "cruel one"). Note adequate. Kept.
- **ἐκταδίην (134)**: see the 134 change; `l` "outstretched", `i` "ample" kept.
- **ἔστρωτο + ῥινόν (155)**: see the 154–155 change. Middle pluperfect.
- **ἀωτεῖς (159)**: `l` "do you slumber", `i` "are you slumbering" follows the table's ἀωτεῖτε "slumber" (Odyssey 10.548, formation not certain); the note already says the formation is not certain. Kept. "Sleep" is reserved for εὕδω.
- **δυσωρήσωνται (183)**: aorist subjunctive in a simile, no κε needed; "keep a troubled watch" is flagged in the note as a guess from the word's parts and context. The note says "taken to mean"; adequate. Kept.
- **βεβίηκεν (145, 172)**: see the 145 change. "has come upon" kept; the same wording at 172 consistent.
- **ὅ τι (142)**: see the 142 change.
- **εἴ τις … καλέσειεν (111)**: εἰ with optative and no apodosis is a wish; "if only someone would" is correct and the note says so. Kept. Same optative at 171 is the potential with κεν, rightly distinguished.
- **"the other" at 162**: changed, see above.

## Considered and refused

- **φίλος (169)**, note calls it a vocative: the Iliad glossary already carries φίλος as a masculine vocative in address (nominative form doing duty), so the label stands. Left.
- **ἐπέστη "stood over me" (l) / "stood beside me" (i), 124**: ἐφίστημι covers both; not a disagreement in sense. Left.
- **οὕτως "In that case" (129)**: interpretive but the note explains it as "since Menelaus has been sent by Agamemnon". Left.
- **ὄφελεν … πονέεσθαι `i` "he ought to be going about" (117)**: slight expansion of πονέεσθαι κατὰ ἀριστῆας … λισσόμενος, but the sense is carried. Left.
- **νεμεσήσεαι (115) as "uncontracted future middle"**: consistent with 129's νεμεσήσεται; the aorist subjunctive alternative gives the same English. Left.
- **κιχησόμεθα, ἠγερέθεσθαι, ἀκαχμένον, κατὰ μοῖραν, ἀμύμων, νήδυμος, πολύμητις, χαλκοχιτώνων, ποικίλον, γεραιέ**: all agree with the table or the published parts (iliad-003/047 for κατὰ μοῖραν at 169; Odyssey 15.551 for 135; line 91 of iliad-058 for νήδυμος; Odyssey 14.131 "old man" for γεραιέ in `i`).
- **Repeated lines**: 102/128/143 equal iliad-024's unit, 119 equals iliad-053's, 144's first line equals 2.173, 163 and 191 equal 1.201 and 4.284 in wording, 178 equals 10.24 (iliad-058); `l` and `i` match the published English in each case.

# Pass 2 — gloss.json

Every parse checked against the line. 135 entries (126 new, 9 broadened). Format checked: no entry over 230 characters, only typographic ’, no line numbers, no "here".

## Changes (form · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

| form | severity | wrong | done |
|---|---|---|---|
| τόσον (broadened) and unit 22 `l`/`n` | major | τόσον is neuter and an adverb ("so greatly"); the pass-1 `l` "need indeed so great" read it as an adjective of χρειώ (feminine). The broadened entry also said "has come" for a present. | `l` now "that need indeed so greatly comes?”"; note says τόσον is an adverb; entry now "comes so greatly". The ὅτι reading of ὅ τι needed no gloss entry (ὅττι already carries conj. ὅτι). |
| ἔστρωτο | major | Parsed as a passive, contradicting the corrected unit note (ῥινόν is an accusative). | "plpf. 3 sg. mid. (+ acc.): ’had spread (for himself)’", noting that the passive has the same form. |
| βεβίηκεν | minor | Asserted βιάω "oppress" as the lemma though the origin is uncertain. | "βιάω (or βιβάω; origin uncertain)", sense "come upon". |
| δυσωρήσωνται | minor | "be sleepless with care" was a guess beyond the evidence; lemma δυσωρέομαι kept (the form is middle). | Sense cut to "keep a troubled watch (rare; sense guessed from context)". |
| ἠγερέθεσθαι | none to entry | Lemma ἠγερέθομαι matches the glossary's ἠγερέθονται. | Entry kept; unit 15's note said ἀγερέθομαι, now ἠγερέθομαι. |
| οἶοι | minor | "’we alone’" did not match the line (second person, addressed to two men). | "’alone’, said of more than one person". |
| πάννυχον | minor | "used as an adverb of time" contradicts the corrected unit 35 note (cognate object). | "agreeing with ὕπνον (a cognate object of the verb)". |
| σαυρωτῆρος | minor | "’by the spike’" for ἐπί + gen. | "’on the spike’". |
| ἀπό | minor | Example "ἀπό τ’ ἀλσέων" is not in this part; the word here is adverbial in tmesis. | Mentions tmesis, example ἀπό τέ σφισιν. |
| κιχησόμεθα | minor | Attic equivalent "καταλήψομεν" is not a form of any tense of the verb. | "καταληψόμεθα". |
| ὄτρυνέ | minor | "impf." against the unit note's aorist; the unaugmented form can be either. | "aor. (or impf.)". |

Counts, pass 2: major 2, minor 9.

Checked and left: νεμεσήσεαι (future, matching 129); ἀμήχανός (matches iliad-047's ἀμήχανα); the nine broadened readings (each keeps the old entry whole; νύκτα, μάχεσθαι, πόνου, ποικίλον, τέ, ὄφελεν, ἐγείρομεν, κλισίης fit their lines); ἐκταδίην (matches the corrected unit note).
